pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the head - Urban Mission School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from Executive Head
I am delighted to welcome you to Urban Mission School and to share with you the opportunities we offer.
We are a warm, supportive, and inclusive community welcoming pupils of all backgrounds and abilities. Whilst every pupil has their own story of why they have come to us, at UMS every pupil starts with a clean slate and our focus is solely on what they do next.
We are incredibly proud of our unique young people, supportive parents and carers, inspirational staff, and collaborative advisory board. These elements all work together to make UMS a safe, secure, happy, stimulating, and enjoyable place to learn.
We are a warm, supportive and inclusive community welcoming pupils of all backgrounds and abilities.
Our vision is to provide an inclusive education within a safe, nurturing environment where children can belong, learn, and succeed. It is built on Christian values that all people are made in the image of God with immense potential.
Young people are at the heart of every decision, and we place vital importance on their physical and emotional well-being. We ensure we provide the best possible personalised curriculum with excellent teaching and learning as key priorities, ensuring that our children/ young people are confident, enthusiastic, and motivated to learn and that the opportunities we provide are relevant to their needs both now and in the future.
Safeguarding our children and young people and promoting their well-being runs through the heart of our practice. Our school’s ethos, values, and beliefs place the well-being of our students at the forefront of all we do. Policies and systems such as: Safer Recruitment, Relationship and Behaviour Management, Access to the Curriculum, Health and Safety within the school and on trips and visits, and Child Protection Procedures all support, promote, and sustain a safe learning and working environment.
We are extremely fortunate to have such a dedicated team of teachers, teaching assistants, counsellors, and other specialist staff who strive to ensure that every young person is equipped with the skills they need to continue their future learning journey. We work with the local community and parents/ carers and very much value the support and contribution they make to school life.
We hope that as you go through our website you will understand the ethos, facilities and opportunities for learning at UMS. If you would like additional information, please contact us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Supporting Parents and carers - Urban Mission School
pageCache.text:
Supporting Parents and Carers
Partnering With You
You want the best for your children and young people, so do we. Rethink the experiences that you’ve had with other schools. We’re not here to cast judgement but to do the best for your child.
There’ll be regular meetings each term where we set targets and check in to see how your child is doing, so we’ll be in touch all the time. Add us to your favourites and call if you’re worried, unsure or delighted with anything that’s going on with your child. The more open we are with each other, the quicker we can deal with issues, find solutions and make progress. We love nothing more than celebrating your children – from little wins to big breakthroughs – you’ll be the first to know. At the end of your child’s final review, you’ll be invited to a special Awards Presentation. We want to mark their time with us, applaud their progress and send them off filled with hope and encouragement.
Supporting You
You are the most important person in your child’s lifeand we want to support you in making sure they achieve their best potential.
We’ll share our experience with you so you can build your child’s resilience and reinforce what they’re learning at school.
You’ll have one key contact, who’ll be your go-to person. They’ve worked with hundreds of families, so whatever you’re facing they’ll be a great source of advice and support.
All we ask is that you’re honest about your challenges and commit to work with us and persevere. We’ve seen remarkable transformations when parents commit to working with us to try a few new things.
Beyond the Curriculum
We’re here to equip your child for life. This means helping them to manage strong emotions, deal with disappointment, build good relationships and speak up for themselves.
To do this, our staff use what we call a holistic approach. This means we’re aware of the additional challenges going on in your child’s life that may stem from trauma or attachment issues.
We approach teaching in a very different way to most schools too. We take a nurturing and therapeutic approach, valuing the overall wellbeing of your child above anything else.
In the classroom, we’re not focused on completing a syllabus, but rather giving your child tools for life. They’ll learn how to work together, give presentations and build relationships with their peers, teachers and other staff. These are skills that will set them up for life.
Giving your child the best means that we have to stay on top of our game too. Our staff stay sharp by keeping up to date with the latest practices, tools and ways of thinking.

Referrers’ Views​​
What Do You Think of UMS?
As someone who has referred a student to UMS, your perspective is incredibly valuable to us. We’re always striving to improve, and your insights can help us understand what we’re doing well and where we can enhance our referral process.
If you have a few minutes to spare, we’d really appreciate if you could complete our quick referrer survey. It’s a friendly, straightforward way for you to share your experiences with us.
Complaints
Addressing Concerns and Feedback at UMS
At UMS, we value your feedback and are committed to addressing any concerns you may have in a timely and effective manner. If there’s something you’re not satisfied with, we encourage you to let us know as soon as possible.
If you have a concern, please don’t hesitate to speak with any member of our staff. They are trained to listen to your feedback, understand the issue, and take the necessary steps to resolve it. Most concerns can be addressed quickly and informally, without the need for a formal complaint process.
If you don’t feel the situation has been resolved, then you can put your complaint in writing and either email it to the school or send a letter.
You can email this to info@umsc.uk or 1 Cornmill Lane, London SE13 7FY.
Our staff will work with you to understand the details of your concern, including any relevant dates, individuals involved, and your desired resolution. They will then investigate the matter and provide you with a response within three business days.
If you feel that your concern has not been adequately addressed or you would like to submit a formal complaint, you can do so in writing. You can email your complaint to info@umsc.uk or send a letter to:
Urban Mission School1 Cornmill LaneLondon SE13 7FY
When submitting a formal complaint, please be as specific as possible about the nature of your concern, including any relevant details, dates, and your desired outcome. This will help us investigate the matter thoroughly and provide you with a timely and appropriate response.
At UMS, we are committed to addressing all concerns and complaints fairly, quickly, and confidentially. We understand that raising a concern can be difficult, and we will treat your feedback with the utmost care and respect.
Our goal is to work collaboratively with you to find a satisfactory resolution. We appreciate you taking the time to share your perspectives, as it helps us continually improve the educational experience for all our students and families.
If you have any questions or need further assistance, please don’t hesitate to reach out to our staff. We are here to support you and ensure your child’s success at UMS.

Working With Referrers​
Referral Process
Contact the Head Teacher directly if you’d like to refer a student to us. Referrals are usually made by schools and local authorities, and sometimes agencies such as Youth Offending Teams and Social Services.
As a referrer, we will ensure you know exactly what’s going on with your student’s attendance, progress, and engagement. We’ll work together to help them make positive progress and achieve success.
When you make a referral, here’s what you can expect
Families are invited to visit the school before any formal admission process starts. We want them to see what we’re all about and what we can offer.
The prospective student, their referrer and parent or carer joins us for an informal interview. We’ll discuss expectations and boundaries, so everyone knows where they stand.
When a student has been accepted, we’re constantly in contact with our referrers. We encourage referrers to ask questions and be part of the journey.
Each term, referrers get a formal progress report and are invited to attend a review where we’ll plan the next steps.
As students approach the end of their placement, we offer additional support and mentoring to help them transition back to mainstream school or start a new placement.
We bring referrers, parents or carers, and students together at the end of the placement to finalise the transition plan and end the placement well.

Our Curriculum​
Education that focuses on the needs of young people and goes beyond the curriculum
Here at UMS, we want our students to be the best version of themselves. Our goal is to empower them academically and socially so that they can become well-rounded individuals.
Our curriculum isn’t a checklist of knowledge, but rather a framework that helps our young people gain the fundamental skills and knowledge they need for life.
Through therapeutic and learning support, we engage our children in all the educational and enrichment activities we offer.
Our teachers are always on the lookout for topics that spark their curiosity. We then develop tailored programs to nurture their talents and passions to help each student reach their full potential.
We prioritise open communication with all parents and carers. We will share your child’s progress through regular phone calls, emails, and in-person meetings so that you are actively involved in their educational journey.
Curriculum Overview
UMS’s ‘Thinking Curriculum’ enables pupils to think critically and creatively. It allows our students to apply the knowledge they learn in one subject to another by developing essential personal and interpersonal skills, alongside their academics.
Our curriculum is diverse and complete encouraging young people to:
Empowering Students Through a Balanced, Enriching Curriculum
Many young people come to us with very low numeracy and literacy skills. So, we find creative ways to boost their confidence and enable them to take control of their learning. In the process, they’ll naturally acquire skills in English and maths and a love of learning.
When it comes to English – we put a big emphasis on reading and getting our young people to expand their vocabulary. Put simply, knowing more words makes you smarter. We encourage our young people to explore words through a whole range of genres.
The approach to maths is similar. We make connections between what they learn in the classroom and its application in real life. When young people can see the relevance, it’s easier to engage them.
Through our focus on English and maths, we introduce a wide range of topics, including RE, History, English, Geography, Science, IT, Citizenship, Media, and Humanities.
We’re ambitious, but we’re also realistic. We set goals that we know our students can reach, and we challenge them to go above and beyond.
Through cross curricular projects, educational trips, activities, outside speakers and residentials help pupils to develop a whole range of additional skills and knowledge. It’s through stimulating and interactive learning that young people develop and maintain motivation.
There’s also a team of experts journeying with each child. Pupils have access to counselling, mentoring, learning and therapeutic support, including speech and language, art, Lego and music therapy.
Young people also love expressing themselves through performing arts and music and rolling up their sleeves to get messy with food tech, design or art and crafts. PE also features heavily, with sport being a wonderful outlet for them and a way to teach resilience and discipline.
We want our young people to gain knowledge and be better thinkers. Alongside individual learning, we get them involved in group work and developing their presentation skills.
Students also develop life and social skills through personal development programmes which help them how to manage anger, make positive choices, develop healthy lifestyles and live independently.
When students are ready, we help them put their learning into practice, through part-time college placements in a vocational area of their choice. We also arrange work experience placements each term to introduce them to the world of work.
Success looks different for each child and isn’t necessarily measured by a GCSE grade. However, we recognise that qualifications open new opportunities to young people.
So, we offer Functional Skills qualifications which are key to helping our young people progress into vocational study, apprenticeships or traineeships and will be offering GCSEs in some subjects as well.
Beyond these set goals, we want to re-engage young people in learning and help them develop those transferrable skills and personal capabilities that will set them up for life.

About UMS
Who We Are
We support the young people other schools are unable to, using innovative teaching methods and personalised support. Why? Because we believe there is innate potential in everyone. And we really do mean everyone. Each pupil that attends UMS has a team of dedicated professionals in their corner to help them throughout their studies.
This is our community. These are our young people. Our future.
UMS’s journey began in 2003 when a group from a local church began supporting young people in the local schools across the area of Lewisham.
Over three decades, we have built a reputation as an organisation that puts the needs of young people first and works tirelessly to help them progress. That objective remains the same today, and will continue to guide us in the future.
Our Vision and Ethos
Driven by our Christian faith, we will not turn our back on those who are struggling, however hard it may be.
We recognise that the traditional education system is challenging for many of our young people. Those carrying emotional burdens or dealing with complex home situations need more help than the average school can provide. That’s where we come in.
As a team of teachers, therapists, psychologists, and mentors, we know how to address emotional needs, behavioural challenges, and academic struggles.
We also understand the burdens and pressures that go with being a young person in London right now.
We build a personalised support team around each child. Their focus is to help each young person work through the tough stuff and develop strategies to confidently step back into mainstream education.
UMS’s purpose is to help young people understand their unique talents, gifts, and responsibilities.
When a young person understands who they are and how they can use their individuality to make a positive impact, lasting change happens.

We're anything but your average school

We’re here for all the children in our community who need us – those who have faith and those who do not.
The values that drive our work are grounded in our Christian belief that all people are made in the image of God with immense potential, free to make choices according to their own convictions.

Managing Behaviour​
We see behaviour as a way of the young people trying to communicate.
Others see our pupils as troublesome – we see them as vulnerable.
Our young people are dealing with some pretty complex stuff. The frustration, anger, hurt or disappointment they harbour can lead students to act out or withdraw completely.
Where others see challenging behaviour, we focus on the reasons why children are responding in a particular way.
With the help of our wider team of mentors and professional staff we help them address these underlying issues and give them the skills to cope with all that life throws at them.
Success looks different for each child. But overall, we want to help them take control of their behaviour so they can confidently transition back into mainstream school with key skills for life.
Our Approach
To achieve all this, we need to start early, think differently and work as a team.
This really starts with attendance. Children and young people need to be in school. Now, this in itself can be tricky, since so many have had such a bad experience of education.
But we’re up for the challenge. Relationships are key. Through small classes, and the one-on-one support of a therapeutic special educational needs coordinator, our counsellor and staff who are trauma-informed, we create places where our students feel safe and well-supported.
What others see as poor choices are often a response to a bigger challenge. But our students still need to know what’s right and wrong.
Boundaries keep children safe, give them a focus, and teach them about consequences. So, we’ve got clear behavioural principles that parents, children, and staff agree on.
When they cross the line, there are sanctions. But we’re consistent, fair, and ready to wipe the slate clean and start again. We all need to know there is forgiveness and a second chance.
Since our young people are dealing with their own challenges, they have individual goals we set together. We start with small targets and build up.
As students learn to control their responses, persevere, or speak up, they feel good. This gives them the buzz they need to keep going.
Children and young people are with us for about one to three terms. We offer both long and short-term placements for our young people and we see the difference in them when they leave or stay.
This all takes persistence and a lot of support along the way. But at UMS behaviour is everyone’s business.
Every member of staff, mentor, support worker or session tutor is focused on helping our pupils to conduct themselves in a way that is productive and positive.
We share all the skills and tools we use with parents and carers to ensure consistency at home and in school.
